subject: Design review: BYOK/KMS operator latency & egress controls
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Carlos Ramirez <c.ramirez@acme.com>
Cc: Acme Security Team <secops@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Design review: BYOK/KMS operator latency & egress controls

Hi all —

Attaching the proposed sketch and a short operator playbook for Acme's private deployment review (attachments: kms-egress-diagram.pdf, operator-playbook.md). This thread is to capture the decisions we need to finalize before the security review and procurement checklist. High-level goals:

- Preserve full BYOK semantics (customer KEKs never leave customer boundary in plaintext).
- Keep HSM interactions low-latency for token signing/unwrap operations (target P99 < 120ms for unwrap in primary site).
- Prevent operator-only access to raw key material; operator actions should be limited to orchestration/rotation signals and auditable sealed-ops.
- Eliminate blind escrow: avoid any long-term raw-key escrow unless mutually pre-agreed escrow and legal controls exist.
- Explicit egress controls: only wrap/unwrap ops allowed to transit a small, audited KMS proxy; wrapped blobs may flow but plaintext must not.

Specific asks from our side:
1) Acme: confirm HSM vendors in-scope (Thales, Utimaco, AWS CloudHSM?) and whether remote HSM-attestation is required.
2) Acme: acceptable SLA/latency envelope for key unwrap calls from the on-prem inference fleet (we propose P50 40ms, P95 80ms, P99 120ms).
3) Internal: feedback on operator separation options (operator only gets unseal tokens for orchestration; key material unsealed only inside HSM enclave).

Design notes (summary):
- Local KMS proxy (customer VPC) performs request routing to HSM in on-prem rack. Proxy keeps ephemeral wrapping keys cached for short TTL (30s) to avoid repeated HSM roundtrips; cache is sealed and requires attested process identity.
- Envelope encryption: model keys are encrypted with per-tenant KEK that only the HSM can unwrap. HSMs do asymmetric wrap so wrapped KEKs can be stored in S3-compatible object store.
- Rotation: automated rolling with overlap window to avoid downtime; rotation orchestrator issues rotation events signed by customer root key.
- Operator actions: operator CLI can request a sealed operation (e.g., rotate node), which results in an attestation check + a signed request to HSM; raw keys never returned to operator.

Please review and flag anything that would be a showstopper for your audit teams. I'll consolidate and drive a final doc for the security questionnaire responses.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: kms-egress-diagram.pdf (diagram), operator-playbook.md (text)
From: Carlos Ramirez <c.ramirez@acme.com>

Cc: Acme Security Team <secops@acme.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Design review: BYOK/KMS operator latency & egress controls

Thanks, Stephanie — good writeup. A few clarifying questions from Acme Security before we escalate to procurement:

1) HSM support: we currently run Thales Luna and are evaluating Utimaco in a second datacenter. We will not be using CloudHSM for our primary cluster. Can Redwood confirm the proxy/HSM control plane supports Luna API and PKCS#11 flows (we need vendor-level compatibility)?

2) Cache TTL: you call out a 30s ephemeral wrapping-key cache. From our side, any cache that can return unwrap results in <120s must be auditable and tied to attestation. Does the cache persist across process restarts? How is the cache sealed to operator access?

3) Audit trail: we require immutable retention for unwrap/sign events for 5 years (hashed evidence acceptable) and must be able to produce a per-event attestation blob for compliance. Is the attestation export in scope?

4) Disaster plan: if the on-prem HSM becomes unreachable, what is Redwood's fallback? Can we fail over to a read-only wrapped-key mode to keep inference running (i.e., continue serving using cached wrapped keys and local cache until HSM is back online)? We need concrete behaviour defined.

We can jump on a quick call if that helps.

—Carlos Ramirez
Head of Security Engineering, Acme Corp
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Ramirez <c.ramirez@acme.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2026 11:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Design review: BYOK/KMS operator latency & egress controls

Carlos — great questions. Short answers and proposed guardrails below. I also attached a quick benchmark summary (benchmark-run-0516.csv) from our HSM lab that demonstrates the latency envelope for typical unwrap/sign ops against a Thales-like emulator.

1) HSM compatibility: we support PKCS#11 + vendor SDKs. Our proxy is pluggable: it implements an adapter layer for Luna and Utimaco. Customer-side deployment will include a vendor adapter module and an attestation script. We'll document exact API calls and recommended firmware versions.

2) Cache TTL and sealing: the ephemeral wrapping-key cache is process-local and keyed by an attested enclave identity. On process restart the cache is empty and requires re-attestation. Cache contents are encrypted with a short-lived ephemeral key derived from the HSM (not operator-managed). Operators can request a cache eviction; they cannot extract cache plaintext. We propose default TTL 30s; we can tune to 60–90s upon request but that increases exposure window.

3) Audit trail: we can emit signed audit events for each unwrap/sign (including measurement of the attestation result). Logs are hashed and pushed to an immutable S3 store with object-lock for retention. We can provide per-event attestation blobs (binary) on export; note: export will include non-secret metadata only. We will work with your legal/compliance on retention policy details.

4) Disaster behaviour: we support two modes configurable by the customer:
   - Strict mode: if HSM unreachable, fail open = false => deny unwraps, inference returns an error (best for highest assurance).
   - Degraded-serving mode: allow serving using cached wrapped KEKs and ephemeral cache for a bounded window (configurable, default 15 minutes). This is auditable and leaves a clear post-mortem attestation trail.

Operational notes:
- Rotation: rolling rotation uses overlapping KEK validity with an overlap window of +N minutes (default N=10) to avoid mid-rotation downtime. Rotation commands are signed by customer root and go through the attested proxy.
- Operator separation: operators only hold orchestration tokens and unseal signals. Raw unwrapped key operations must be performed by an attested process which has undergone local hardware attestation.

If these items look ok, Stephanie and I can update the doc and produce a short checklist for Acme's auditors.

—Vivek
Sr. Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

1) Redwood: produce a vendor compatibility appendix (Thales + Utimaco) and a short attestation export guide (owner: Vivek) — target 2026-05-21.
2) Acme: confirm desired degraded-serving window if you want something other than default 15 minutes (owner: Carlos).
3) Redwood: add detailed audit-export example and retention matrix for your legal team (owner: Mina) — target 2026-05-22.
4) Internal: runway to security review doc + fill questionnaire answers (owner: Stephanie) — draft by 2026-05-24.

I'll schedule a 30 min sync for Thursday 10:00 AM PDT to walk the appendix and the fallback semantics. If you need a different time, flag it.

One note: we will not run any long-term private escrow by default — if Acme wants escrow, we'll need a signed escrow agreement and a short architecture addendum describing legal gate and key custody controls.
